rationale: Starting from scratch, I designed a balanced robot geometry with 5 sensors spread evenly across the front to detect the tape line effectively. I chose a medium sensor size (0.012 m) to balance resolution and coverage. The wheel track and body width are set to 0.12 m to allow stable turning without excessive width that would increase off-track risk. The wheel radius is 0.035 m for a good compromise between speed and torque, and the mass is 0.8 kg to keep inertia manageable. The controller uses a moderate base speed of 1.2 to encourage fast progress without risking instability. PID gains are set to moderate values (kp=8, ki=0.5, kd=3) to provide responsive but stable steering. Sensor weights are arranged to steer left when the left sensors detect the line and right when the right sensors do, with the center sensor weighted highest for strong centering. The line loss strategy is 'last_direction' to continue turning in the last known direction to recover the line. I request a broad set of observations including completion, progress, errors, line loss events, and control effort to understand performance and guide future tuning. This initial design aims for a stable, responsive robot that can complete the track with minimal line loss and error, providing a solid baseline for iterative improvement.
